paper_metadata.title: Effects of alloying elements on phase stability in Nb-Si system intermetallics materials

evidence.quote: The effects of alloying elements, such as Ti, Cr, Al and Hf on phase stability in Nb eSi system intermetallics materials have been investigated

Small alloy button ingots were prepared by arc melting under an argon atmosphere on a water-cooled copper hearth, using a non-consumable tungsten electrode. The alloy buttons were melted at least 3 times to assure the chemical homogeneity of constituent elements.

evidence.quote: The larger particles (about 10 mm) are the primary-Nb phases formed during solidiﬁcation and the ﬁner particles (about 1 mm) are the secondary-Nb phases formed during the eutectic reaction.

the microstructure consisted of the dispersed dark particles in the continuous matrix, and the result of EDS analysis indicated that the dark phases are Nb 5Si3 phases, suggesting that Al addition can promote the direct formation of equilibrium Nb 5Si3 phase.

For the alloys with Hf and Ti additions (alloys 4# and 5#, Fig. 2 (c),(d)), the results of EDS analysis showed that the microstructure consisted of Nb solid solution and Nb 3Si matrix, similar to that of Nb eSi binary alloy. However, the morphologies of component phases in alloys with Hf and Ti additions are different from the binary alloy, a great amount of dendrite Nb phases occurring.
